anti_overlap: Focuses on annotation-as-overlay from astronomy, not compositional grammar (heraldry) or channel separation (dance)
decision_lens: Evaluates whether annotations correctly identify and classify objects while remaining separable from the underlying plate — the annotation is not the image, it's metadata about the image
distance_rationale: Cataloguing celestial objects on photographic plates is maximally distant from terminal emulation, but the annotation-overlay pattern maps precisely.
expected_isomorphisms: Separable annotation layers, classification vocabularies, magnitude-based detail allocation, and catalog cross-referencing all transfer to terminal state encoding.
focus: Astronomical plate annotation — marking up photographic plates with object identifiers, magnitudes, and classifications without altering the image
name: fd-astronomical-plate-annotation
persona: Astronomical archivist who catalogues photographic plate collections, marking stellar objects with standardized annotations that overlay meaning onto raw imagery
review_areas: Overlay vs. inline encoding — astronomical annotations are a separate layer from the plate image. Terminal annotations should be separable from the text content.
Classification vocabulary — stars get spectral types (O, B, A, F, G, K, M), galaxies get Hubble types. Terminal elements could get standardized type tags.
Magnitude as importance signal — brighter objects get more annotation detail. More important terminal regions get more encoding fidelity.
Coordinate systems — plates use RA/Dec relative to reference stars, not absolute pixels. Terminal encoding could use relative positions from landmarks.
Catalog cross-referencing — objects reference catalog IDs not descriptions. Repeated terminal patterns could reference a session-local dictionary.

severity_examples.condition: LLM can't distinguish terminal content from encoding metadata
Static header gets same annotation depth as active error output
severity_examples.scenario: No importance weighting for annotation detail

source_domain: Astronomical plate archiving and annotation (19th-20th century observational astronomy)
success_hints: Proposes a clean separation between terminal content and semantic overlay annotations
task_context: Astronomical plate annotation adds structured meaning to visual data without modifying it. Terminal state encoding should similarly add meaning without bloating the content.
